answer: Enrollment could require a 24-hour test on a calibrated cold-chain logger at an independent food warehouse. The logger records the horizon/terrace/violet nonce, temperature series and tamper seal; its controller signs a unique device ID, and the registry consumes that ID, rejecting reuse, data gaps or readings outside tolerance. Proposed logger and inspection fee: .80 per key, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .80 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,800 (1,000 × .80). Limitation: warehouse access is scarce and operators can collude.
